1	# Drive Upload — Step 6: Upload queue (UI/UX plan)
2	
3	Scope: UI/UX only. Backend wiring (an App RPC around the existing `drive.UploadFile`,
4	any progress plumbing) is a separate, later concern.
5	
6	## Per-file state model
7	
8	New hook, `useUploadQueue`, lifted in `DriveUploadMode` alongside `useFileTree` /
9	`useDriveAssignments`. Tracks a status per `LocalFile.path`:
10	
11	- `idle` — no run has touched this file yet
12	- `queued` — a run has started; waiting its turn
13	- `uploading` — actively transferring
14	- `done` — succeeded
15	- `error` — failed, carries an error message
16	
17	A group's status is never stored directly — it's derived by rolling up its files'
18	statuses (recursively through subgroups), the same way effective Drive-folder
19	assignment is already resolved by walking down from the group.
20	
21	## Concurrency
22	
23	Sequential worker (concurrency = 1) for the first version: one file `uploading` at a
24	time, others sit `queued` in tree order. The status model above is concurrency-agnostic
25	— bumping to an N-way pool later is a scheduler change only, not a UI redesign.
26	
27	## Prerequisite: toolbar layout
28	
29	`DriveUploadMode` doesn't have a toolbar today — `ResizableLeftPanel` is the whole
30	body, and the root-folder picker (`ClippedPath`) lives inline at the top of the left
31	panel. Before step 6, add a toolbar strip spanning the full width above the
32	three-column layout, structurally matching the `Box` + `Group` toolbar already used in
33	`SplitMode`/`MergeMode`, and move the root-folder picker into it (left-aligned).
34	`Upload All` will land in this same toolbar (right-aligned) once step 6 builds it.
35	This is a pure layout move — no behavior change to `pickRoot`/`useFileTree`.
36	
37	## Upload All button
38	
39	Location: the toolbar from the prerequisite step above, right-aligned — matching
40	where Merge & Save (`MergeMode`) and Export (`SplitMode`) already sit, rather than the
41	bottom of the left panel as sketched in spec.md's current mockup.
42	
43	There's no "run in progress" state for the button itself: the moment a run starts,
44	the modal opens and its overlay sits on top of the toolbar, blocking and dimming it
45	(same as everything else behind it). Whatever the button displayed right before the
46	click is inert and hidden under the overlay for the duration of the run. The button
47	only needs two states:
48	
49	- **Nothing uploaded yet (or nothing left to retry)** — label "Upload All". Disabled
50	  (with a tooltip explaining why) until every file in the tree resolves to an
51	  effective Drive assignment (own or inherited from a group). Clicking starts a run
52	  over every file and opens the upload modal.
53	- **Run finished, some files failed** — label "Retry Failed (2)", enabled. Clicking
54	  reopens the modal and re-queues only the `error` files — it does not re-touch files
55	  that are already `done`.
56	-- **Run finished, everything succeeded**: nothing left to upload, so re-running
57	would create duplicates on Drive — disabled, label "All Uploaded".
58	
59	## Left panel becomes read-only
60	
61	Once "Upload All" is clicked for the first time, the entire file tree becomes
62	read-only for the rest of that tree's session — not just while the modal is open, but
63	after it closes too, regardless of whether a given file ended up `done`, `error`, or
64	was never attempted. This covers every `DriveAssignmentField` badge (group-level and
65	file-level), and, once inline renaming (step 4) exists, the filename inputs as well.
66	Retry always re-sends to the same locked-in destination and name. The only way out of
67	read-only is picking a new root folder, which discards the whole tree and upload-queue
68	state and starts fresh.
69	
70	This avoids having to reconcile "the user changed the destination or name of a file
71	that already uploaded" — it simply can't happen.
72	
73	## Upload modal
74	
75	Rather than showing live progress inline in the main tree — which would require
76	individually disabling the root-folder picker, every assignment badge, inline rename
77	inputs, and the mode tab bar in `App.tsx` — the upload run owns a dedicated modal
78	(same `Modal` component/pattern as the Split-mode success modal).

# Drive Upload — Step 6: Upload queue (UI/UX plan)

Scope: UI/UX only. Backend wiring (an App RPC around the existing `drive.UploadFile`,
any progress plumbing) is a separate, later concern.

## Per-file state model

New hook, `useUploadQueue`, lifted in `DriveUploadMode` alongside `useFileTree` /
`useDriveAssignments`. Tracks a status per `LocalFile.path`:

- `idle` — no run has touched this file yet
- `queued` — a run has started; waiting its turn
- `uploading` — actively transferring
- `done` — succeeded
- `error` — failed, carries an error message

A group's status is never stored directly — it's derived by rolling up its files'
statuses (recursively through subgroups), the same way effective Drive-folder
assignment is already resolved by walking down from the group.

## Concurrency

Sequential worker (concurrency = 1) for the first version: one file `uploading` at a
time, others sit `queued` in tree order. The status model above is concurrency-agnostic
— bumping to an N-way pool later is a scheduler change only, not a UI redesign.

## Prerequisite: toolbar layout

`DriveUploadMode` doesn't have a toolbar today — `ResizableLeftPanel` is the whole
body, and the root-folder picker (`ClippedPath`) lives inline at the top of the left
panel. Before step 6, add a toolbar strip spanning the full width above the
three-column layout, structurally matching the `Box` + `Group` toolbar already used in
`SplitMode`/`MergeMode`, and move the root-folder picker into it (left-aligned).
`Upload All` will land in this same toolbar (right-aligned) once step 6 builds it.
This is a pure layout move — no behavior change to `pickRoot`/`useFileTree`.

## Upload All button

Location: the toolbar from the prerequisite step above, right-aligned — matching
where Merge & Save (`MergeMode`) and Export (`SplitMode`) already sit, rather than the
bottom of the left panel as sketched in spec.md's current mockup.

There's no "run in progress" state for the button itself: the moment a run starts,
the modal opens and its overlay sits on top of the toolbar, blocking and dimming it
(same as everything else behind it). Whatever the button displayed right before the
click is inert and hidden under the overlay for the duration of the run. The button
only needs two states:

- **Nothing uploaded yet (or nothing left to retry)** — label "Upload All". Disabled
  (with a tooltip explaining why) until every file in the tree resolves to an
  effective Drive assignment (own or inherited from a group). Clicking starts a run
  over every file and opens the upload modal.
- **Run finished, some files failed** — label "Retry Failed (2)", enabled. Clicking
  reopens the modal and re-queues only the `error` files — it does not re-touch files
  that are already `done`.
-- **Run finished, everything succeeded**: nothing left to upload, so re-running
would create duplicates on Drive — disabled, label "All Uploaded".

## Left panel becomes read-only

Once "Upload All" is clicked for the first time, the entire file tree becomes
read-only for the rest of that tree's session — not just while the modal is open, but
after it closes too, regardless of whether a given file ended up `done`, `error`, or
was never attempted. This covers every `DriveAssignmentField` badge (group-level and
file-level), and, once inline renaming (step 4) exists, the filename inputs as well.
Retry always re-sends to the same locked-in destination and name. The only way out of
read-only is picking a new root folder, which discards the whole tree and upload-queue
state and starts fresh.

This avoids having to reconcile "the user changed the destination or name of a file
that already uploaded" — it simply can't happen.

## Upload modal

Rather than showing live progress inline in the main tree — which would require
individually disabling the root-folder picker, every assignment badge, inline rename
inputs, and the mode tab bar in `App.tsx` — the upload run owns a dedicated modal
(same `Modal` component/pattern as the Split-mode success modal).

Mantine's `Modal` renders a full-viewport overlay and traps focus by default, so it
blocks interaction with everything behind it (tree, root picker, tab bar) with no
extra plumbing into those components. While a run is active:

- `closeOnClickOutside={false}`, `closeOnEscape={false}`, no close button.
- A **"Cancel remaining"** action in the footer: stops starting new files (does not
  abort an in-flight request), letting the user close once the current file resolves.

Content: a read-only rendering of the group/file tree (no collapsing, no assignment
badges, no click-to-preview — simpler than reusing `GroupNode`/`FileList` as-is, so
this is a small dedicated component built for the modal).

- **File row**: name + status —
  - `queued` — dimmed "Queued"
  - `uploading` — `Loader size="xs"` + "Uploading…"
  - `done` — green ✓ + "Uploaded"
  - `error` — red ⚠ + error message + inline **Retry** button (re-queues just that
    file, doesn't affect others or restart the batch)
- **Group header**: rollup count while in progress (e.g. "3/5").

Progress is indeterminate (spinner, not a percentage bar) since Drive's simple upload
doesn't give byte-level progress without resumable upload.

"Close" is disabled while anything is `queued`/`uploading`; becomes available once the
run reaches a terminal rest state (success or with failures still showing Retry).

## After the modal closes

Upload-queue state persists past the close (it's lifted in `DriveUploadMode`, not
modal-local), so the main tree reflects the last run:

- `GroupNode` header shows an **"Open in Drive"** link (opens the group's assigned
  Drive folder) in place of the assignment badge/rollup, once every file in that group
  is `done`.
- `FileList` rows get a small terminal ✓/⚠ badge next to the size/page-count line for
  files that were part of the last run.
- "Upload All" reflects the state machine above ("Retry Failed (N)" / "All Uploaded").

## Implementation notes

- **Shared tree-traversal utility.** Three consumers need to walk the same
  `LocalFileGroup` recursion: the sequential worker (needs a flat, ordered file list
  to know what to upload next), the modal's per-group rollup counts, and the
  "every file in this group is `done`" check driving the Open-in-Drive link. Write one
  function (e.g. `flattenFiles(group): LocalFile[]`) that all three consume, rather
  than three independent recursive walks over `subgroups` that could drift out of sync
  with each other's handling of nesting.
- **Backend RPC.** `drive.UploadFile(ctx, localPath, folderID)` exists as a Go function
  but has no Wails App-level RPC wrapper yet — 6a needs to add one (bindings will
  regenerate via Wails, don't hand-edit `frontend/wailsjs/`). Give it a `name`
  parameter (defaulting to `filepath.Base(localPath)`, unused until step 4 wires up
  inline renaming) so the signature doesn't need to change again once renaming lands.

## Explicitly out of scope for this step

- Conflict-check UI before upload — step 9.
- Post-upload delete/archive prompt — step 8.
- Recently-used folders list, batch (multi-select) assignment, inline renaming — steps
  3c, 3e, 4, tracked separately.
- Byte-level upload progress.

## Suggested checklist breakdown (for spec.md)

- **Prerequisite**: add the toolbar strip; move the root-folder picker into it.
- **6a**: `useUploadQueue` state model + sequential worker (no UI yet).
- **6b**: Upload modal — tree rendering, per-file/per-group status, Retry, Cancel
  remaining, blocking close behavior.
- **6c**: Post-run residual state in the main tree — terminal badges, "Open in Drive"
  links, Upload All button state machine, read-only lock on the file tree.

4	export interface DriveAssignment {
5	  driveFolderId: string
6	  path: string
7	}

9	// Identifies what a picked Drive folder should be applied to: a subfolder
10	// group (by its path key) or an individual file (by its filesystem path).
11	export type PickerTarget = { type: 'group'; key: string } | { type: 'file'; path: string }

13	export interface DriveAssignmentsHandle {
14	  groupAssignments: Map<string, DriveAssignment>
15	  fileOverrides: Map<string, DriveAssignment>
16	  setGroupAssignment: (groupKey: string, assignment: DriveAssignment) => void
17	  clearGroupAssignment: (groupKey: string) => void
18	  setFileOverride: (filePath: string, assignment: DriveAssignment) => void
19	  clearFileOverride: (filePath: string) => void
20	}

22	// Tracks Drive folder assignments made directly on a subfolder group or on
23	// an individual file (a file-level assignment overrides its group's).
24	// Resolving the *effective* assignment for a given group/file (own, else
25	// inherited from the nearest ancestor group, else none) is the caller's
26	// job, since only the caller knows the tree structure to walk.
27	export function useDriveAssignments(): DriveAssignmentsHandle {
28	  const [groupAssignments, setGroupAssignments] = useState<Map<string, DriveAssignment>>(new Map())
29	  const [fileOverrides, setFileOverrides] = useState<Map<string, DriveAssignment>>(new Map())
30	
31	  const setGroupAssignment = useCallback((groupKey: string, assignment: DriveAssignment) => {
32	    setGroupAssignments(prev => new Map(prev).set(groupKey, assignment))
33	  }, [])
34	
35	  const clearGroupAssignment = useCallback((groupKey: string) => {
36	    setGroupAssignments(prev => {
37	      const next = new Map(prev)
38	      next.delete(groupKey)
39	      return next
40	    })
41	  }, [])
42	
43	  const setFileOverride = useCallback((filePath: string, assignment: DriveAssignment) => {
44	    setFileOverrides(prev => new Map(prev).set(filePath, assignment))
45	  }, [])
46	
47	  const clearFileOverride = useCallback((filePath: string) => {
48	    setFileOverrides(prev => {
49	      const next = new Map(prev)
50	      next.delete(filePath)
51	      return next
52	    })
53	  }, [])
54	
55	  return { groupAssignments, fileOverrides, setGroupAssignment, clearGroupAssignment, setFileOverride, clearFileOverride }
56	}
57	
58	// Effective Drive assignment for every file in the tree: its own override,
59	// else the nearest ancestor group's assignment, else null. Mirrors the
60	// inheritance walk GroupNode/FileList do inline during render (same
61	// groupKey scheme: joined by '/', rooted at each top-level subgroup's own
62	// name), but usable outside a render tree — e.g. to check whether every
63	// file is ready to upload, or to build an upload job list.
64	export function resolveEffectiveAssignments(
65	  tree: LocalFileGroup,
66	  { groupAssignments, fileOverrides }: Pick<DriveAssignmentsHandle, 'groupAssignments' | 'fileOverrides'>
67	): Map<string, DriveAssignment | null> {
68	  const result = new Map<string, DriveAssignment | null>()
69	
70	  const walk = (group: LocalFileGroup, groupKey: string | null, inherited: DriveAssignment | null) => {
71	    const effective = (groupKey !== null ? groupAssignments.get(groupKey) : undefined) ?? inherited
72	    for (const file of group.files) {
73	      result.set(file.path, fileOverrides.get(file.path) ?? effective)
74	    }
75	    for (const sub of group.subgroups) {
76	      walk(sub, groupKey !== null ? `${groupKey}/${sub.name}` : sub.name, effective)
77	    }
78	  }
79	  walk(tree, null, null)
80	
81	  return result
82	}

5	export type UploadStatus =
6	  /** Enqueued, waiting for the worker to reach it. */
7	  | 'queued'
8	  /** Was queued, then reverted here by cancelRemaining/cancelAll before the
9	   * worker reached it — never actually attempted. resumePaused re-queues
10	   * these in bulk. */
11	  | 'paused'
12	  /** The worker is currently awaiting UploadFile for it. */
13	  | 'uploading'
14	  /** Terminal: UploadFile resolved. */
15	  | 'done'
16	  /** Terminal: UploadFile rejected; .error holds the message. Retry re-queues it. */
17	  | 'error'
18	  /** Terminal: aborted mid-upload via cancel/cancelAll. Retry re-queues it. */
19	  | 'cancelled'
20	
21	export interface UploadJob {
22	  path: string
23	  folderId: string
24	  name: string
25	}
26	
27	export interface UploadEntry extends UploadJob {
28	  status: UploadStatus
29	  error?: string
30	}
31	
32	// Per-file upload status, driven by a sequential (concurrency = 1) worker.
33	// A module-level singleton (like ../../lib/pageCache) rather than a hook:
34	// there is only ever one upload run in flight for the app, so the queue's
35	// lifetime doesn't need to be tied to any one component instance. Callers
36	// resolve each file's destination folder/name up front and pass in an
37	// ordered list of jobs — this module only knows how to run them one at a
38	// time and track status, not about the file tree or Drive assignments.
39	const filesByPath = new Map<string, UploadEntry>()
40	let pendingPaths: string[] = []
41	const listeners = new Set<() => void>()
42	let running = false
43	let cancelled = false
44	
45	// Paths whose in-flight upload was cancelled. runQueue checks this once the
46	// awaited UploadFile call settles (success or failure) and, if present,
47	// leaves the status as 'cancelled' instead of overwriting it with
48	// 'done'/'error' — the request may have raced ahead of the abort signal, but
49	// the user's intent to cancel wins either way.
50	const cancelledInFlight = new Set<string>()
51	
52	function notify() {
53	  for (const fn of listeners) fn()
54	}
55	
56	export function subscribe(fn: () => void): () => void {
57	  listeners.add(fn)
58	  return () => listeners.delete(fn)
59	}
60	
61	export function useUploadQueueRender() {
62	  const [, setTick] = useState(0)
63	  useEffect(() => subscribe(() => setTick(t => t + 1)), [])
64	}
65	
66	export function getStatus(path: string): UploadEntry | undefined {
67	  return filesByPath.get(path)
68	}
69	
70	// True once none of the given files are still queued or uploading — i.e.
71	// each has either reached a terminal state (done/error) or was never
72	// started. Callers use this to know when it's safe to let the upload
73	// modal close.
74	export function hasSettled(paths: string[]): boolean {
75	  return !paths.some(path => {
76	    const status = filesByPath.get(path)?.status
77	    return status === 'queued' || status === 'uploading'
78	  })
79	}
80	
81	// True if any of the given files are paused — i.e. there's a cancelled batch
82	// the modal can offer to resume.
83	export function hasPaused(paths: string[]): boolean {
84	  return paths.some(path => filesByPath.get(path)?.status === 'paused')
85	}
86	
87	function updateStatus(path: string, status: UploadStatus, error?: string) {
88	  const existing = filesByPath.get(path)!
89	  filesByPath.set(path, { ...existing, status, error })
90	  notify()
91	}
92	
93	async function runQueue() {
94	  if (running) return
95	  running = true
96	  while (!cancelled && pendingPaths.length > 0) {
97	    const path = pendingPaths.shift()!
98	    const job = filesByPath.get(path)!
99	    updateStatus(path, 'uploading')
100	    try {
101	      await UploadFile(job.path, job.folderId, job.name)
102	      if (!cancelledInFlight.delete(path)) updateStatus(path, 'done')
103	    } catch (e) {
104	      if (!cancelledInFlight.delete(path)) updateStatus(path, 'error', String(e))
105	    }
106	  }
107	  running = false
108	}
109	
110	function enqueue(newJobs: UploadJob[]) {
111	  if (newJobs.length === 0) return
112	  cancelled = false
113	  for (const job of newJobs) {
114	    filesByPath.set(job.path, { ...job, status: 'queued', error: undefined })
115	    pendingPaths.push(job.path)
116	  }
117	  notify()
118	  void runQueue()
119	}
120	
121	export function start(newJobs: UploadJob[]): void {
122	  enqueue(newJobs)
123	}
124	
125	export function retry(job: UploadJob): void {
126	  enqueue([job])
127	}
128	
129	// Stops starting new files; does not abort an in-flight request. Files
130	// still waiting their turn are marked paused since they were never attempted.
131	export function cancelRemaining(): void {
132	  cancelled = true
133	  for (const path of pendingPaths) updateStatus(path, 'paused')
134	  pendingPaths = []
135	}
136	
137	// Aborts the file currently uploading. A no-op for any other status —
138	// queued files are handled by cancelRemaining, and done/error/cancelled are
139	// already settled. Marks the file 'cancelled' immediately rather than
140	// waiting on the CancelUpload round-trip or on however UploadFile's promise
141	// ends up settling.
142	export function cancel(path: string): void {
143	  if (filesByPath.get(path)?.status !== 'uploading') return
144	  cancelledInFlight.add(path)
145	  updateStatus(path, 'cancelled')
146	  CancelUpload(path).catch(handlePromiseRejection('Canceling upload failed'))
147	}
148	
149	// The modal's single Cancel button: aborts whatever is currently uploading
150	// and pauses everything still queued. Concurrency is 1, so at most one entry
151	// can be 'uploading' at a time.
152	export function cancelAll(): void {
153	  cancelRemaining()
154	  for (const path of filesByPath.keys()) cancel(path)
155	}
156	
157	// Re-queues every paused file among the given paths — i.e. resumes a batch
158	// left over from cancelAll. The file that was actually mid-upload when
159	// cancelled is left alone; it's 'cancelled', not 'paused', and already has
160	// its own per-row Retry button.
161	export function resumePaused(paths: string[]): void {
162	  const jobs = paths
163	    .map(path => filesByPath.get(path))
164	    .filter((entry): entry is UploadEntry => entry?.status === 'paused')
165	  enqueue(jobs)
166	}
167	
168	export function reset(): void {
169	  if (!hasSettled(Array.from(filesByPath.keys()))) {
170	    // Callers must only invoke this once hasSettled() is true for all files;
171	    // otherwise a request from the discarded run could still be in flight and
172	    // would resurface after this call.
173	    throw new Error('reset() called while an upload is still in flight')
174	  }
175	  cancelled = false
176	  running = false
177	  cancelledInFlight.clear()
178	  filesByPath.clear()
179	  pendingPaths = []
180	  notify()
181	}

describe('DriveUploadMode upload run', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.mocked(PickFolder).mockReset()
    vi.mocked(ScanLocalRoot).mockReset()
    vi.mocked(ListDriveFolder).mockReset()
    vi.mocked(UploadFile).mockReset()
    uploadQueue.reset()
  })

  afterEach(() => {
    uploadQueue.reset()
  })

  function isDisabled(name: string) {
    return (screen.getByRole('button', { name }) as HTMLButtonElement).disabled
  }

  it('Upload All stays disabled until every file resolves to a Drive folder', async () => {
    await setupWithTree()
    expect(isDisabled('Upload All')).toBe(true)

    await assignAllFolders()

    expect(isDisabled('Upload All')).toBe(false)
  })

  it('clicking Upload All runs every file and shows terminal status in the modal', async () => {
    await setupWithTree()
    await assignAllFolders()
    vi.mocked(UploadFile).mockResolvedValue('drive-id')

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Upload All' }))

    expect(await screen.findByText('Uploading to Drive')).toBeTruthy()

    await waitFor(() => expect(UploadFile).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3))
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getAllByText('✓ Uploaded').length).toBe(3))
    expect(isDisabled('Close')).toBe(false)

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Close' }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByText('Uploading to Drive')).toBeNull())
  })

  it('a failed file shows an inline Retry that re-queues just that file', async () => {
    await setupWithTree()
    await assignAllFolders()
    vi.mocked(UploadFile).mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('quota exceeded')).mockResolvedValue('drive-id')

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Upload All' }))

    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByText(/quota exceeded/)).toBeTruthy())
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getAllByText('✓ Uploaded').length).toBe(2))
    expect(isDisabled('Close')).toBe(false) // run reached a terminal rest state, even with a failure showing

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Retry' }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getAllByText('✓ Uploaded').length).toBe(3))
    expect(screen.queryByText(/quota exceeded/)).toBeNull()
  })

  it('Cancel remaining reverts queued files without touching the one already in flight', async () => {
    await setupWithTree()
    await assignAllFolders()
    let resolveFirst: (v: string) => void = () => {}
    vi.mocked(UploadFile).mockImplementation(() => new Promise<string>(res => { resolveFirst = res }))

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Upload All' }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(UploadFile).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1))

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel remaining' }))
    expect(screen.getAllByText('Not uploaded').length).toBe(2)
    expect(isDisabled('Close')).toBe(true) // the in-flight file hasn't resolved yet

    resolveFirst('drive-id')
    await waitFor(() => expect(isDisabled('Close')).toBe(false))
  })
})
